The inherited guidance already narrows the useful baseline: the `0.70/0.35` direct-turn damping pair and `10°/25°` bearing geometry are the supported anchor, while extra static bias merely advances the same failing upper loop. I’m now comparing the full sampled sheets and diagnostics to choose one orthogonal, bounded intervention.

The wake-reading skill now requires direct image inspection before any edit. I’m checking the common held-fish prewarm first, then the best finite rollout (`11°` bias) against the informative `10°` anchor and the two regressions.

The comparison is decisive at the mechanism level: all four sampled policies self-propel upstream but trace the same broad upper loop, and neither more yaw damping nor a steeper bearing map changes the exit. The inherited phase-selective descendant also lost much of the anchor’s approach performance, so I’m documenting a narrower posterior-servo target-limit hypothesis before touching the controller.

The skill’s required diagnosis and durable evidence distillation are now in place. The single candidate restores the supported steering anchor and adds one `40°` posterior target margin; I’m checking the exact diff and then invoking the mandated lightweight check-runner (no CFD).
